home.title: Fairclock — fair meeting times across time zones, weekends & holidays
home.description: Find a meeting time that works for your whole team: time zones, Friday–Saturday or Saturday–Sunday weekends and public holidays in 200+ countries. Free, no sign-up.
home.h1: Meeting times that are fair to everyone
home.lead: Add your teammates' cities. Fairclock shows when everyone is in working hours, and it also knows that Friday is the weekend in Riyadh and that Diwali is a holiday in Mumbai.
home.content:
Why another time zone tool?

Classic converters only answer “what time is it there?”. Real teams also have different weekends, public holidays, and colleagues who always end up taking the 7 a.m. or 10 p.m. call. Fairclock puts all of this in one view.

  • Weekends that differ by country. Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait and Egypt rest on Friday and Saturday, most countries on Saturday and Sunday, Iran on Friday only. Fairclock applies the right weekend to each person, and you can change it.
  • Public holidays. National holidays for 2026–2028 in more than 200 countries appear in the grid and in the “Days off ahead” list.
  • Fairness. When no time works for everyone, Fairclock proposes two alternating weekly slots, so the inconvenience is shared instead of always falling on the same people.
  • Privacy by design. No account and no server: your team lives in the share link and in your browser.

How to use it

  1. Type a city and pick it from the list. Your own city is added automatically.
  2. Open “Hours & weekend” on a card to adjust working hours or weekend days.
  3. Click an hour in the grid, or one of the best times, to see everyone's local time. Copy the invite text or download a calendar file.
  4. Copy the share link and send it to your team. They will see the same plan in their own language.

Frequently asked questions

Does Fairclock handle daylight saving time?

Yes. Times are calculated with the official time zone database built into your browser, so clock changes, which happen on different dates in North America, Europe and the southern hemisphere, are always taken into account.

Where do the public holidays come from?

From the open-source holidays library, which tracks official national calendars. Regional holidays (a single state or province) and company-specific days off are not included. Islamic holidays depend on the sighting of the moon and can move by a day.

What does “fair” mean here?

Each half hour gets a cost for each person: zero inside working hours, a little just before or after, a lot at night, on a weekend or on a public holiday. The best time is the one where the worst cost for any single person is lowest, then the total. For recurring meetings, Fairclock looks for two slots whose combined cost is spread as evenly as possible.

Is it really free?

Yes, free and without sign-up. The site is funded by advertising.
